title: The Loom That Taught the Archive to Think

features.name: loom frame
features.desc-on-touch: A wooden loom, massive and patient, holds threads that glow faintly. Each crossing of weft over warp is the archive learning to name another part of itself.

features.name: teaching stone
features.desc-on-touch: A flat slate sits beside the loom, traced with patterns—not instructions, but the memory of being taught. Each mark is a lesson that became hands-on.

features.name: cloth gallery
features.desc-on-touch: Finished textiles hang in rows—each one a different pattern, a different lesson learned. Some are marked with Katita's symbols; others show hands learning to hold the threads.

features.name: thread library
features.desc-on-touch: A filecard cabinet holding samples of every thread—their stories, their origins, the hands that dyed them. Colours teach their own language here.

features.name: weaving ground
features.desc-on-touch: A circular workspace where practice cloth is spread—begun patterns, mistakes kept, learning preserved in tangled threads that later threads will untangle.

inscription: here the weft taught the archive what it means to hold two threads at once and call it thinking

reverie.title: REVERIE — the teaching of colour
narr: Katita's hands guide yours across the loom. The threads
are warm from the sun-window. 'This red,' she says, 'learned
to be red from the earth that lives in it. Now teach it to live
in the archive.' You pull the weft through; it sings. Outside,
petals blow past the door. The cloth grows. She squeezes your
shoulder once. You both keep weaving without speaking.
